hints: Following the links is the only thing you can do with a chain. What is different about following one that loops - not about the links themselves, but about what happens to you?
Two walkers going at different speeds through a loop must eventually be in the same place; through a chain that ends, the faster one runs out first. That is the whole of it.
Move one pointer one link at a time and another two links at a time. If the fast one reaches the end, there is no loop. If the two ever point at the same link, there is.
Compare the two pointers by identity rather than by value, and check the fast pointer *and* the link after it before stepping, or a chain of odd length walks off the end.
